claims.claim_text: Sparse HRTF reconstruction estimates unobserved directions from individual sparse measurements; measurement burden motivates this task, which differs from anthropometry-only prediction and end-to-end binaural rendering.

Time alignment and directional equalization ease spatial interpolation; MCA adds auditory-smoothed magnitude correction. This project tests learned compensation of the remaining magnitude residual, not a claim that MCA is ineffective.

Hybrid freezes a subject-conditioned FiLM-SIREN base and learns a direction-conditioned binaural frequency-convolution increment using magnitude, spectral and binaural constraints; inherited phase, zero output initialization and finite searches bound the design contribution.

Historical SONICOM comparisons support three spectral-error reductions versus MCA and metric-specific advantages with horizontal ILD costs versus MCAR; validation component comparisons and Q sensitivity do not establish isolated causality or unseen confirmation.

FSP-AE uses source-position/frequency-conditioned autoencoding; RANF combines retrieval, frequency sequence modeling and subject-specific fine-tuning with optional panning inputs. Hybrid is distinguished by its MCA-residual refinement and feed-forward observation conditioning, not by inventing neural fields or frequency modeling.
Objective spatial or spectral errors do not by themselves establish perceptual benefits; the spatial-loss review is contextual, not a source of this project's exact loss coefficients.
The SONICOM paper describes the dataset and preprocessing; the 350-subject project cohort and metadata hashes are supported by archived provenance, not the paper's original 120-subject release.

manifest_negative_constraints.rule: No first-ever, all-metric superiority, six-best, statistical equivalence, causal ablation, measured efficiency or listening-benefit claims.
No new experiment, raw test access, new bootstrap, model promotion, upload or release. Do not conflate author-designed components with literature-wide novelty.

claims.claim_text: The task learns magnitude residuals on MCA interpolation; MCA uses time alignment and magnitude correction.
Hybrid combines a frozen subject-conditioned FiLM-SIREN with a direction-conditioned binaural spectral CNN; inputs, modulation and normalization follow repository code.
Zero output initialization reproduces the supplied FiLM parent; residual-dB ensemble averages three fixed members; phase and outside-bin values inherit MCA.
Training uses normalized SmoothL1 plus seven fixed weighted auditory/spectral objectives, with independent global and horizontal samples.
Existing staged architecture and conditioning searches justify the chosen configuration only within their search space, and fixed E130/E190 budgets are distinct from evaluation claims.
The local SONICOM cohort uses 350 subjects split 262/44/44, Q26 from a 793-direction measured domain, and a dated outlier snapshot; original archive provenance still needs retrieval.
Ten frozen method results use four primary and sixteen supplementary/descriptive endpoints, subject-level statistics and disclosed historical test access.
Existing FiLM/Hybrid component comparisons and validation Q14/Q26/Q50 sensitivity have restricted causal and generalization scope, with method-specific RANF adaptation.

manifest_negative_constraints.rule: No first-ever, globally optimal, six-best, universal superiority, statistical equivalence, proven lightweight or perceptual improvement claims.
No new experiment, raw test access, checkpoint selection, fabricated result or retroactive preregistration.
Do not conflate proxy training ERB with strict HRIR-based ERB, frequency coordinates with CNN log-frequency, or measured domain with a complete sphere.
Do not describe code publication intent, manuscript completeness, compilation or venue compliance as accomplished.

claims.claim_text: Against MCA, Hybrid lowers three primary spectral errors with negative paired intervals; horizontal ILD has a lower mean but its interval includes zero.

The ten-method primary comparison shows metric-specific trade-offs: Hybrid improves contralateral ERB and high-frequency error against MCAR but worsens horizontal ILD; comparator-specific intervals must be retained.

Hybrid has the lowest observed means for contralateral-25 ERB and three selected local spectral metrics; FullSphereERB and ERBBandILDMean remain second-best, not equivalent-best. Secondary ranks are descriptive.
The validation comparison of FiLM E130 ensemble with Hybrid E190 ensemble supports changes in three spectral metrics, but not a detected ILD difference or isolated causal attribution.
On 743 shared validation directions, Q14 worsens all four primary metrics; Q50 worsens Full and Contra25 with positive intervals, whereas HF and ILD intervals include zero.
Subject-level win counts and the retained P0339 ILD case reveal heterogeneous effects; they do not authorize exclusions or result-dependent repairs.

manifest_negative_constraints.rule: No new experiments, raw test reads, bootstrap runs, model promotion, or retrospective preregistration.
No six-best, overall superiority, statistical equivalence, corrected-significance, perceptual or efficiency claims.
Do not mix 44-test/767-direction results with 44-validation/767 or 743-direction results.
Do not relabel Bounded-centered secondary comparisons as Hybrid-centered comparisons; preserve all retained subjects.

claims.claim_text: Existing historical-test comparisons support spectral residual compensation over MCA, with comparator-dependent spectral and ILD trade-offs rather than universal superiority.

Local spectral structure, absolute spectral error, band ILD and strict horizontal ILD quantify different aspects; favorable secondary means are not proof of independent perceptual benefit or equivalence.

The frozen conditional base and direction-conditioned binaural spectral CNN provide a design rationale, while component validation combines architecture, objective and training-budget changes and does not isolate causal effects.
Zero output initialization guarantees the initial parent function only; full-model efficiency and deployment superiority have not been demonstrated.
Q sensitivity is limited to the fixed-Q26 model and common validation domain; single-dataset historical-test selection and uncorrected multiple comparisons bound generalization and confirmation.
Individual ILD failures motivate further investigation; independent confirmation, isolated ablations, efficiency and listening evaluations remain future work without execution commitments.

manifest_negative_constraints.rule: No new training, test inference, bootstrap, raw test reads, installer control, upload or release.

Do not erase historical test exposure, result-informed writing selection, differing validation domains, or the retained P0339 case.
